meta.source: HubSpot MCP connector — search_properties / get_properties / query_crm_data / tool_guidance
meta.note: type_source='verified' means fetched via get_properties; 'inferred' means derived from the label and must be confirmed before filtering on it.

derivation_rules.name: ENUM-VALUE MATCH
derivation_rules.rule: If the user's phrase equals or contains an enumeration option VALUE or LABEL of a property, that property wins. 'QVault TPM IoT' is an option of prod___product_name_new_ → filter that property with the exact value. Highest confidence.

derivation_rules.name: LABEL MATCH
derivation_rules.rule: Match the phrase to the business LABEL (incl. prefixes 'PROD -', 'OPP CUST -', 'INFO -', 'DATE -'), not the internal name. 'Sales region' → INFO - Sales Region → sales_region.

derivation_rules.name: GOVERNANCE PRECEDENCE
derivation_rules.rule: Prefer the governed property: label/description says '(new)' or 'only use this from now on'. Demote '(USE ONLY IF EXCEPTION)', '(DO NOT USE)', '(IGNORE)', 'TEST', 'to_delete', 'Test Property'. product_name and solution_family__new_ are never the default answer.

derivation_rules.name: YEAR-BY-LABEL
derivation_rules.rule: For any (metric, year) phrase — pipeline / cumulative pipeline / weighted / volume / weighted volume / services value / ASP — resolve through the LABEL. Several internal names were recycled (weighted_2021_calculation is 'Weighted 2027 (k$)'; asp_in_usd_q2_2022_calculation is 'ARR ($K/Y)'). Use the Year Resolver sheet.

derivation_rules.name: TYPE PREFERENCE
derivation_rules.rule: enumeration > bool > number > free-text string. For money aggregation always use amount_in_home_currency / hs_projected_amount_in_home_currency; never SUM(amount) across currencies. Display amount together with deal_currency_code.

derivation_rules.name: STATE SHORTCUTS
derivation_rules.rule: won / lost / open / closed → hs_is_closed_won / hs_is_closed_lost / hs_is_closed (booleans, pipeline-independent). Only use dealstage IDs when the user names a specific stage AND pipeline (IDs are pipeline-specific; 'Design Win' has 6 different IDs).

derivation_rules.name: NAME-LIKE FALLBACK
derivation_rules.rule: dealname LIKE '%x%' is a LAST RESORT, only when no enum option matches, and the answer must be flagged approximate. Never use it for product/category questions — it under-counts (2 vs 32 for QVault TPM IoT).
derivation_rules.example: dealname LIKE '%Qvault%'  ← wrong for product counts

derivation_rules.name: ASSOCIATION
derivation_rules.rule: 'company / account / contact of the deal' → cross-object OBJECT.property in SELECT/WHERE (COMPANY.name, CONTACT.email). Existence checks → associations.OBJECT IS NOT NULL (WHERE only). Max 2 associated objects per query.

derivation_rules.name: SELF-REFERENCE
derivation_rules.rule: 'my / I / me / mine' → hubspot_owner_id = <resolved owner id> (resolve via user-details). Without it the query returns the whole account.

derivation_rules.name: TIME WINDOW DEFAULTS
derivation_rules.rule: 'this year' = 2026-01-01..2026-12-31; 'this quarter' = 2026-07-01..2026-09-30; 'last quarter' = 2026-04-01..2026-06-30; 'last 90 days' = since 2026-06-16. Dates use BETWEEN with 'YYYY-MM-DD' strings, never timestamps.

derivation_rules.name: AMBIGUITY
derivation_rules.rule: If two governed properties both match (e.g. 'TPM' hits product_hierarchy=TPM, product_line=TPM and prod___product_name_new_ in {QVault TPM, QVault TPM IOT}), pick the most specific level the user named (SKU > line > family) and state the alternates.
derivation_rules.example: TPM → product_line unless a SKU was named

hubsql_rules.rule: One object per query: DEAL, COMPANY, CONTACT, TICKET, CALL, MEETING, NOTE, TASK (upper-case). No JOIN / UNION / subqueries / CTEs.
Plain property names only. NOT supported: DISTINCT, AS aliases, CASE WHEN, IF(), string functions (CONCAT/UPPER…), COALESCE.
Aggregate on amount_in_home_currency / hs_projected_amount_in_home_currency. Display amount with deal_currency_code.
Operators: =, !=, <, >, <=, >=, LIKE '%x%', IS NULL, IS NOT NULL, IN (...), BETWEEN 'YYYY-MM-DD' AND 'YYYY-MM-DD'.
hs_is_closed = false / true (unquoted). Custom yes/no enums are quoted strings and case-sensitive ('YES', 'Yes', 'true').
Filter on the option VALUE, not the label (pipeline = '12096408', not 'SealSQ Hardware'; dealstage = '12096412').
BETWEEN with date strings, not timestamps. DATE_TRUNC(prop, 'DAY'|'WEEK'|'MONTH'|'QUARTER'|'YEAR') in SELECT and GROUP BY.
COUNT(*), SUM, AVG, MIN, MAX, MEDIAN. No HAVING. No COUNT(DISTINCT x) → use GROUP BY x + COUNT(*).
SELECT COMPANY.name FROM DEAL … / WHERE COMPANY.industry = 'X'. Existence: WHERE associations.DEAL IS NOT NULL (WHERE only). Max 2 associated object types per query.
'my/I/me' → hubspot_owner_id = '<owner id>' resolved from user details; otherwise the query covers the whole portal.
ORDER BY col ASC|DESC, LIMIT n.
Confirm names with search_properties; confirm enum values with get_properties; then query.
